test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A ladder is leaning against a wall such that it makes an angle of 60° with the ground. If the length of the ladder is 10 metres, how far is the foot of the ladder from the wall?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90°** right-angled triangle, the sides are in the ratio **1 : √3 : 2**.

The side opposite to **30°** (base distance) is always **half** of the **hypotenuse** (ladder length).

Distance = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 metres.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **ladder (Hypotenuse)** = 10 metres

**Angle of inclination** with ground (θ) = 60°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29388e3dac970ea4c7896fcb0ac3afed26bfba4f0a5bdf14aa62f01a72f13960.png] 

**Formula Used:**

cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos 60° = Distance from wall ÷ Length of ladder

⇒ 1/2 = Distance ÷ 10

⇒ Distance = 10 × (1/2)

⇒ Distance = 5 metres

**∴ The correct answer is 5 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

For a right-angled triangle: sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse, and tan θ = Perpendicular/Base.

Common Values

cos 30° = √3/2, cos 45° = 1/√2, cos 60° = 1/2, and cos 90° = 0.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².</p
